claims.text: The powder feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy alloy.
The build platform should be maintained at 600–800°C during additive manufacturing.
Build-platform preheating reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-platform preheating reduces residual stress in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-platform preheating reduces process-induced defect formation.
Reducing segregation, residual stress, and defects improves mechanical integrity relative to room-temperature-platform processing.
The proposed comparison uses an inert atmosphere and holds laser power, scan speed, and other processing parameters constant.
Platform preheating produces a more homogenized microstructure.
Platform preheating reduces compositional segregation at grain boundaries.
Elevated substrate temperature reduces the cooling rate during solidification.
The reduced cooling rate and thermal gradients limit diffusion-driven segregation associated with rapid localized solidification.
Slower cooling permits stress relaxation between deposited layers.
Residual stresses contribute to defect formation.
Preheated samples will exhibit at least a 25% reduction in residual stress relative to room-temperature-platform samples.
Preheated samples will have a more uniform grain structure and fewer segregation features.
Preheated samples will have improved tensile and fatigue properties.
Room-temperature-platform additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces higher residual stress, notable segregation, and degraded mechanical performance.
The intervention is expected to remain effective only below the onset temperature of deleterious phase transformations and under a controlled inert atmosphere.
The optimal preheat temperature and resulting effects may vary among additive-manufacturing setups, and long-term service stability remains unvalidated.
